pr_title: Refactor ERR codes 2 (without the Hurd specific bits)
pr_body:
This fixes a series of current problems with the ERR sub-system:

-   reason codes overlaps
-   known issues with recorded system errors (they get truncated to 24 bits, previously even fewer), which we now detect and skip over
-   look through a larger range of system errors, to try and catch them all (even though POSIX allows any number that fits in an **int**, most systems use a range within 1..255)

Fixes #12276
Fixes #12217
Fixes #12354
pr_comments: The ideas mentioned in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/12314#issuecomment-652801232 are now implemented here.  @DDvO, please have a look.

Travis failures (on tests) are relevant.

BTW, nice to see the improved (by #12279) semantics of `VF=1` at work also for the Travis CI :)
Ewwww, that parallel testing output looks quite ugly.  Hardly legible
Ah, I see why.  Some macros need to be converted to static inline functions to avoid multiple evaluation of the argument

> Ewwww, that parallel testing output looks quite ugly. Hardly legible

This is to be expected on arbitrarily interleaved output of parallel runs.
We should be able to improve on this by buffering all per-test output and then printing it atomically.
Looking at the current state of `run-tests.pl`, this should already be mostly so for for `VF=1` and `VFP=1`,
while for `V=1`, which is not explicitly printed there, I did not check.

My comment above comment was referring to a different aspect: verbose output on failed test cases only.

> Ah, I see why. Some macros need to be converted to static inline functions to avoid multiple evaluation of the argument

Just noticed this - I can have a look at the improved version later ...
This pull request is ready to merge

Merged

issue_context.title: hurd failure
issue_context.body:
On hurd we're getting the following error:
```
04-test_err.t ...................... 
# The results of this test will end up in test-runs/test_err
1..1
    # Subtest: ../../test/errtest
    1..4
    ok 1 - preserves_system_error
    ok 2 - vdata_appends
    ok 3 - raised_error
    # ERROR: (string) 'expected == p' failed @ ../test/errtest.c:56
    # --- expected
    # +++ p
    #    0:- ':error::system library:test_print_error_format:Operation not per'
    #    0:+ ':error::system library:test_print_error_format:(os/kern) invalid'
    #                                                        ^^^^^^^^^ ^^^^^^^
    #   64:- 'mitted:errtest.c:30:'
    #   64:+ ' address:errtest.c:3'
    #         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    # 
    not ok 4 - test_print_error_format
../../util/wrap.pl ../../test/errtest => 1
not ok 1 - running errtest
```
comments: (POSIX doesn't stipulate specific errno numbers, but rather macros, to get the correct errno, see https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/errno.h.html)

Debian's hurd porterbox seems to be unreachable currently, so I
can test it. I suggest you just make a PR for it.
